fix_subject: fix(worktrees): pause retirement at btrfs reservation pressure (#202563)
user_saw: On a btrfs host, background deletion of a retired worktree built up around 100 GiB of metadata reservations, which could stall other writers such as the Gateway's database.
summary: The retired-worktree deletion worker now reads its filesystem's btrfs metadata bytes_may_use counter and pauses unlinking at 40 GiB of reservations, resuming below 20 GiB.
reasoning: This is the third step in a series of pacing mitigations (#192909, #202197, now #202563). Each one bounds a different signal of btrfs metadata pressure from deleting very large trees. The prior worker's 128-entry/8 MiB batches with commit-time and PSI checks worked as designed, but the PR shows those signals do not bound btrfs delayed-reference reservations. That is filesystem behavior at large tree sizes, not a line that broke, so no in-repo commit can be quoted as the cause. One could argue #202197 (58dbe4055043) was an incomplete fix, but it never claimed to cap reservations ('not a calibrated btrfs transaction or latency limit'), so I don't name it as the cause.

fix_subject: fix: PostgreSQL sessions fail to load model context when a transcript has an unpaired surrogate escape (#194591)
cause_quote: The PostgreSQL port of the transcript readers added jsonPathValue as `sql`(${value}::jsonb #>> ${objectPath(path)})`` and used it throughout the model-context projection, so any stored event with an escaped lone surrogate or NUL fails the jsonb cast (22P02).
user_saw: On a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway, every follow-up turn in a session whose transcript held a lone surrogate escape failed with 'invalid input syntax for type json', and a user message containing NUL was dropped.
summary: Routes all PostgreSQL transcript and session-context reads through the jsonNativeFieldsValid (pg_input_is_valid jsonb) guard, decoding rejected rows in JavaScript, and replaces NUL with a space in the full-text index text.
reasoning: SQLite always accepted these escapes; the failure exists only on the PostgreSQL engine, whose transcript readers were made portable in #171545 by casting stored JSON text to jsonb (jsonPathValue, jsonArrayElements, jsonSetPath in json-values.ts plus the model-context projection), so the defect shipped with that port rather than being broken later. The later guard from #183560 covered only some readers; the FTS NUL failure belongs to the same port series, so confidence is medium on the single cause commit.

fix_subject: fix(cua): recover failed resource initialization (#192001)
cause_quote: The new file added `const resources = () => (resourcesPromise ??= createCuaExecutionResources(options));` and dispose awaited `(await resourcesPromise).dispose(discard)`, so a rejected initialization promise was cached and rethrown forever.
user_saw: After a temporary failure creating the CUA resource directory, recording retries and closing the computer execution kept failing with the original error even once the filesystem was repaired.
summary: Clears the memoized CUA execution-resources promise when initialization rejects so the same execution can retry recording or close.
reasoning: GraphQL blame beyond the graft shows the memoized `resourcesPromise ??=` line came from the recording feature 079bb341 (#124035, file added), with 94a06613 (#124156) only dropping the options argument; the feature cached rejections from the start. The fix wraps the same promise in a catch that resets it, matching the reported stuck retry/close.

The fix is an architectural off-main-thread move with accepted CPU/latency costs, so it is classified latent rather than a regression or never-worked; one could also argue not-a-defect (performance hardening), but there was a real reported stall.

Medium confidence because #185581 (2026-11-02) suggests Gemini-path requests with this shape were being sent without a reported 400 until 2026-11-10, so a provider-side enforcement change (latent) cannot be ruled out, and the fix was verified only against a stand-in.

cause_quote: #189847 replaced the border-drawn spinners (e.g. `border: 1.5px solid color-mix(...)`; `border-top-color: currentColor`) with `background: currentColor; mask: var(--spinner-mask);` on the same element that runs `animation: btn-spinner-spin`.

fix_subject: fix(ai): keep provider checkpoints across model switches (#200208)
cause_quote: The server-compaction replay match introduced in openai-responses-compaction-replay.ts included `state.model === context.model &&`, so a checkpoint written by one model was never replayed after a model switch.
user_saw: Sessions that switched models (fallbacks, overrides, alternation) dropped their server compaction checkpoint, resent the full raw history and fell back to client summarization.
summary: Removed the model id from the provider replay fence so compaction checkpoints and replay items survive model switches within the same provider API, endpoint and session.
reasoning: GraphQL blame puts the removed `state.model === context.model` line in #135727 (ef681015), a refactor that moved the fence; #200063's description says the fence was added in #120457, and that PR's diff (47f78a32) adds `state.model === context.model &&` to the original compaction replay match. Server compaction therefore never survived a model switch from the start, which the incident host saw on 357 of 800 dropped-checkpoint turns. The fence was a deliberate conservative choice, now relaxed after raw API checks showed providers accept cross-model items; that makes the not-a-defect reading arguable, so cause confidence is medium.

fix_subject: fix(anthropic): cancelled Claude login checks orphan Claude Code's refresh lock (#197032)
cause_quote: #137071 made probeClaudeCliAuthStatus async and cancellable, passing `signal: params?.signal` with `killProcessTree: true` to runUtf8CommandWithTimeout, so a cancelled caller SIGTERM/SIGKILLs `claude auth status` mid-refresh.
user_saw: The first Claude CLI turn after an idle period stalled about 10 seconds or failed with 'another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh'.
summary: The Claude CLI auth probe no longer forwards the caller's abort signal to the child process; a cancelled caller waits for `claude auth status` to exit on its own, so Claude Code's OAuth refresh lock is released.
reasoning: The removed line `signal: params?.signal` blames to 2640154 (#137071), whose diff shows it replacing a synchronous spawnSync probe (no caller cancellation, SIGTERM-only timeout) with the async cancellable runner, so the cancel-kill path shipped with the defect. Medium rather than high because the failure also depends on Claude Code's `auth status` refreshing tokens under a lock, which I could not confirm existed at that time (if it came later this would lean latent).

fix_subject: fix(codex): preserve native launch errors on Node 24 (#200900)
cause_quote: It bumped `"@openai/codex": "0.164.0"` to `"0.169.0"`, whose launcher uses process.execve, and taught the observer only the structured form (`/syscall: ['"]execve['"]/` plus a matching `path:` line), which Node 24 never prints because it aborts with SIGABRT and a bare `process.execve failed with error code ...` header.
user_saw: On Node 24, a bundled Codex executable that could not run produced a generic app-server startup failure instead of the actionable executable-permission/missing-binary error.
summary: The managed Codex launcher observer now recognizes Node 24's fatal `process.execve failed with error code X` header together with a SIGABRT exit and records it as the native spawn failure.
reasoning: Native launch-error attribution worked with the 0.164 launcher (spawn-style exit-1 diagnostics, #154489/#161419); the PR names #200784 as related, and that commit's diff bumps Codex to 0.169.0 (an execve-based launcher) while adding only the Node 26 structured execve branch, so on Node 24 the diagnostic was lost and the real-launcher tests failed in the hourly Codex shard right after. It could also be read as latent (upstream launcher change with #200784 as trigger), but the in-repo bump and its incomplete adaptation are one commit, so I call it a regression with medium confidence.

reasoning: Blame of every removed assertPrivate line points to 3c34fff (#146616), which created update-candidate-plugin-repair.ts and the private-only target assertion; at that commit update-candidate-plugin-tree.ts already projected host links to the candidate root (`relocations.push({ sourceRoot: host, destinationRoot: candidateRoot })`, `hostLinks`), so the conflict existed from the start. reasoning: Before 3d7f8fbf (#182516) nested Agents/Workflows with a parent_task_id were owner=false and never held; that commit introduced holding children of held parents, with the parent-held check evaluated in one pass in snapshot order, which is exactly the ordering defect fixed here. fix_subject: fix(gateway): requests go unanswered when a teammate is copied (#196571)
cause_quote: The new isHumanAddressedChatMessage returned true for any message with selected mentions whose remaining text did not name the agent (`if (!params.mentions?.length) return false;` then only an agent-name check), so `Please make poster previews. cc @Bob` skipped the agent turn.
user_saw: A chat request that copied a teammate (for example ending in 'cc @Bob') got no agent reply at all.
summary: Treats a message as human-addressed only when it starts with a selected person, so incidental or cc mentions after a request still run the agent.
reasoning: Before ba6dce8d054d, selected human mentions did not suppress the agent, so requests with a cc mention were answered. That commit added isHumanAddressedChatMessage and wired chat.send to skip the agent turn whenever any person was selected and the agent was not named; its diff and docs ('A message with selected people is addressed to them, not to the agent') show the over-broad rule that suppressed cc'd requests, and the fix narrows it to leading mentions. The fix landed the day after, and ba6dce has no PR number in its subject.

fix_subject: fix(sandbox): reduce filesystem stalls after commands (#200787)
cause_quote: #196662 replaced 'Changed checkpoints still pause through capture and publication' with btrfs checkpoints that 'take a filesystem snapshot, then resume', adding `prepareLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture`/`removeLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture` to every changed command checkpoint in runLocalWorkspaceProjection.
user_saw: On a btrfs host running sandboxed agents in large workspaces, the Gateway stalled: SQLite waits of 9 to 19.6 seconds and RPC p99 of about 52 seconds while command checkpoints created and deleted filesystem snapshots.
summary: Changed sandbox command checkpoints now pause the guest and capture directly into an immutable Git result, removing the per-checkpoint btrfs snapshot creation and retirement and the size/duration snapshot selector.
reasoning: Before 10d67445fbe, changed checkpoints paused and captured directly, which is the state this fix restores. That commit introduced a btrfs snapshot plus recursive removal for every changed checkpoint, and per the fix PR each snapshot forces a filesystem-wide btrfs transaction commit that stalled Gateway SQLite in production. d7f90ec35cf (#196727, retire captures, select snapshots only for large or slow trees) and 8ff37a6828b (#198128, skip the freeze) tuned the same path but kept snapshots for exactly the large workspaces that stalled. Medium confidence: the stall mechanism depends on btrfs kernel behavior and production timings I could not verify, and the fix is framed as an owner-accepted trade-off (about 290 ms of extra guest pause) rather than a pure bug fix.

fix_subject: fix(gateway): avoid unused workspace fingerprint reads (#194693)
user_saw: Nothing visible; workspace snapshot reads loaded fingerprint blobs they did not use, with no measured user-facing cost.
summary: The workspace manifest snapshot query now selects only the fingerprint column the scan, probe or archive action needs and returns null for the unused one.
reasoning: This is a performance optimization: the reader has selected both fingerprint columns since it was written (blamed to #184581), and the PR reports no failure and no measured production cost. Nothing became slower than before, so it is not a defect.

fix_subject: fix: stop unavailable chat widgets from flooding history reads (#202220)
cause_quote: It subscribed the widget to gateway events and, whenever `!state.view` and a `chat` event reached state `final`/`aborted`/`error` for the session, ran `forgetPendingCanvasView(binding); activeBinding = undefined; reconcile();`, re-requesting even widgets that had already failed terminally.
user_saw: An old chat with a missing Canvas widget kept offering Retry and re-requested the failed view on every later chat event or remount, and those requests scanned the transcript and slowed other users' history reads.
summary: Control UI now keeps terminal Canvas widget failures across remounts and later chat events and caps transient retries with exponential backoff; the server reads the document before the transcript receipt scan and marks sandbox-host startup failures retryable.
reasoning: The event-driven re-read that floods history reads was added by #175025 (pending/access-denied/host-failure states) and fired for any widget without a view, including terminal unavailable errors; later refactors (#176457, #183467) only moved this logic into the loader/owner modules. The fix also bundles a server-side ordering optimization and a sandbox-failure classification, so the single cause is medium confidence.
